page.title: Hopin alternatives for virtual events
page.description: Compare RingCentral Events, Zoom Events, Airmeet, StreamYard and West Peek Live to find the right virtual event platform for your needs.
page.h1: What are the best Hopin alternatives for virtual events?
page.definition: Hopin alternatives are virtual event platforms that replace Hopin after its acquisition by RingCentral, offering live streaming, networking, registration and analytics for webinars, conferences and hybrid gatherings. They support branded stages, audience interaction tools, sponsor booths and integration with marketing automation.
page.quick_answer: Start by matching your event size and budget to a cost model, then test the top two platforms with a short pilot before committing.

sections.h2: Which platforms replace Hopin for large conferences?

blocks.p: RingCentral Events, Zoom Events, Airmeet, StreamYard and West Peek Live are the leading replacements for large conferences. Ten platforms compared below cover self‑serve streaming studios up to enterprise event suites, each offering branded stages, networking lounges, sponsor booths and analytics dashboards.

sections.h2: What cost models do the main alternatives use?

blocks.p: Three cost models dominate the market: per‑host licences sized by attendee capacity, self‑serve monthly plans, and annual contracts quoted by sales. Choosing a model depends on event frequency, budget predictability and the need for dedicated support.

ul: Per‑host licences sized by attendee capacity (Zoom Webinars)
Annual contracts quoted by sales (ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast)

sections.h2: How do I decide between a self‑serve studio and an enterprise suite?

blocks.p: Match the decision to team size, production complexity and the level of custom branding you require. A structured evaluation keeps the choice objective and avoids feature overload.

ol: List the must‑have features for your event
Score each platform on those features
Run a short pilot with a single session
Review attendee feedback and internal workload
Select the platform that meets the score threshold

sections.h2: When is a production partner needed instead of just software?

blocks.p: The platform is not the production; someone still has to own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready. Software alone cannot manage on‑site cameras, encoder integration or live show calling.

ul: Complex multi‑stage agendas with simultaneous tracks
Hybrid venues requiring on‑site cameras and encoder integration
High‑stakes executive summits where a live producer manages Q&A and backup
Limited internal staff to operate the platform during the event

sections.h2: What timeline should I plan for a virtual summit?

blocks.p: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final. A clear schedule prevents last‑minute gaps in rehearsal, backup stream setup and attendee communication.

ul: Run full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before
Technical check sixty minutes before go live
Send replay within twenty four to forty eight hours

faq.q: How much does a moderated webinar production cost?
faq.a: A moderated webinar typically ranges from two thousand five hundred to seven thousand five hundred dollars per production, covering a live producer, Q&A moderation, branded slides, backup stream and edited recording. The fee also includes speaker briefing, rehearsal coordination and post‑event clip delivery.

faq.q: What is the difference between platform licensing and production services?
faq.a: Platform licensing provides the software for streaming, registration and analytics, while production services supply the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream needed to execute a polished live experience. Both purchases are separate and should be budgeted independently.

faq.q: How far in advance should I book a hybrid conference venue and platform?
faq.a: Lock the venue AV and the event platform at least six to eight weeks before the event date, then finalize the agenda and speaker contracts within the next two weeks. This buffer allows time for technical rehearsals, backup stream setup and attendee communication.

faq.q: Can I run a virtual summit without a dedicated production team?
faq.a: A simple single‑track summit can be managed by one producer handling the platform, speaker cues and Q&A, but multi‑track or hybrid events usually require a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator. Assess internal capacity before deciding to outsource any role.
